Module: chunkkeys

Source: src/zarrcurator/chunkkeys.py

This module contains helpers for parsing zarr chunk keys.

Functions

parseChunkKey()

Parse the chunk coordinates from a chunk key relative to its variable.

Supports zarr v2 keys separated by ‘.’ (0.1) or ‘/’ (0/1), and zarr v3 keys with the ‘c’ prefix separated by ‘/’ (c/0/1) or ‘.’ (c.0.1).

Args: str: Chunk key relative to the variable directory. Returns: tuple: Chunk coordinates, or None if the key is not a chunk key.

Distributor

Distribute the list of tuples of type (variable ,size) into different sub groups, either equal size or based on target size specified by user etc.

Methods of Distributor

  • setFrequencySubGroupDict(): To set the frequency subGroup dictionary directly from JSON file. To set frequencySubGroupDict directly, if for example, loaded from JSON file from an earlier run of ‘zarrcurator’. Args: frequencySubGroupDict[dict]: Dictionary of the frequencies and subGroups. Returns: None.

  • getFrequencySubGroupDict(): To get the frequency subGroup dictionary directly. To get frequencySubGroupDict directly, if for example, from utils of ‘zarrcurator’. Args: None. Returns: frequencySubGroupDict[dict]: Dictionary of the frequencies and subGroups.

  • updateFrequencyGroupDict(): To create the dictionary per frequency and it’s groups. For storing the file sizes and counts for each zarr store per frequency in a dictionary. Args: None. Returns: None.

  • updateFrequencySubGroupDictWithSingleZarrStore(): To update the sub group dictionary per frequency with single subgroup of type ‘zarr’. For initializing each of the zarr stores (per freq and healpix) in the sub group dictionary with sub group of type ‘zarr’, if the size of the entire zarr store is less than the target size. Args: None. Returns: None.

  • updateFrequencySubGroupDictWithTargetSize(): To update the sub group dictionary per frequency with subgroups of size as per target size. For updating each of the zarr stores (per freq and healpix) in the sub group dictionary with sub group whose size is greater than the target size and splitting the sub groups into more subgroups if larger than the target size. Args: None. Returns: None.

  • groupStoreEntries(): To group the entries of a zarr store with nested groups into units that are kept together. For stores with nested groups (e.g. written from an xarray DataTree), the entries are named by their path from the store root, e.g. ‘z2/ocean/sst’. A group whose entries in total fit the target size is kept together as one unit, a larger group is split into its own entries and its sub groups, which are handled the same way. Entries at the store root are units of their own, so for a store without nested groups every entry is a unit. Args: dict: Entry name -> {‘size’, ‘count’} for the entries of a zarr store. Returns: list[tuple]: (list of entry names, total size) per unit.

  • split_zarr_into_equalSized_bins(): To update the sub group dictionary per frequency with subgroups of size as per target size. For updating each of the zarr stores (per freq and healpix) in the sub group dictionary with sub group whose size meets the target size and splitting the sub groups into more subgroups if larger than the target size. Args: obj:. Returns: None.

  • redistributeSubGroups(): To redistribute the subgroups. For redistributing each of the zarr stores (per freq and healpix) in the sub group dictionary based on each of the sub group and it’s size in comparison with the target size,by splitting the sub groups into more subgroups if their size is larger than the target size. Args: obj: None. Returns: None.

  • updateDimensionsToSubGroups(): To update the dimensions to the subgroups. For each of the sub group dictionary based on it’s type, for the ‘var’ and ‘chunk’ types, the dimensions of the original zarr store are to be appended, so that the tar ball is self-contained and could be utiized by the downstream applications. Args: obj: None. Returns: None.

  • getZarrstoreDimensions(): To get the coordinate variables of the zarr store. For getting the coordinate variables of the original zarr store, which are to be appended to the tar balls. These are the dimension coordinates (arrays named after a dimension, e.g. ‘time’ or the HEALPix ‘cell’), the auxiliary coordinates listed in the ‘coordinates’ attribute and the variables named in the ‘grid_mapping’ attribute. Dimension names are read from ‘_ARRAY_DIMENSIONS’ (zarr v2) or ‘dimension_names’ (zarr v3). For stores with nested groups (e.g. written from an xarray DataTree), the coordinates used by the arrays of each of the given groups are collected. As a group can use the coordinates of its parent groups, each coordinate is looked up in the group itself first and then in its parents up to the store root. Args: str: Frequency of the model data. str: Path to the location of the zarr store. list[str]: Group paths relative to the store root, e.g. [‘z2/ocean’]; defaults to the root group ‘’. Returns: list: sorted list of (coordinate variable path, size) tuples.

  • update(): To update the distributor object with the data obtained from the distribution of the input zarr stores. The distributor object will be updated either by scanning each of the zarr stores in the input experiment path, if starting afresh or use the JSON file created from a previous distribution of the experiment. Args: None. Returns: None.

Module: storetree

Source: src/zarrcurator/storetree.py

This module contains helpers for walking the group hierarchy of a zarr store, e.g. a store written from an xarray DataTree, with nested groups.

Functions

isZarrGroupDir()

Check whether a directory is a zarr group.

A zarr v2 group holds a ‘.zgroup’ file, a zarr v3 group a ‘zarr.json’ file with node_type ‘group’. Array directories and plain directories are not groups.

Args: path[str]: Path of the directory. fs[object]: fsspec file system object for object stores, None for local stores. Returns: bool: True if the directory is a zarr group.

listArrayPaths()

List the paths of all arrays in a zarr group and its sub groups.

Works for zarr v2 and v3 groups, with or without consolidated metadata.

Args: group[zarr.Group]: Opened zarr group, usually the root of the store. Returns: list[str]: Sorted array paths relative to the group, e.g. [‘time’, ‘z2/ocean/sst’].

groupAncestors()

List the groups enclosing a store member, from the root down.

Args: path[str]: Path of the member relative to the store root, e.g. ‘z2/ocean/sst’. Returns: list[str]: Group paths relative to the store root, ‘’ being the root, e.g. [‘’, ‘z2’, ‘z2/ocean’].

Module: synthetic_store

Source: src/zarrcurator/synthetic_store.py

Synthetic Zarr experiment generator for zarrcurator.

This module creates local Zarr stores with predictable naming and metadata so core zarrcurator workflows can be tested end-to-end.

Examples: python -m zarrcurator.synthetic_store –output-dir tests/data/synthetic_experiment python -m zarrcurator.synthetic_store –output-dir tests/data/synthetic_experiment –run-smoke python -m zarrcurator.synthetic_store –output-dir /tmp/layouts –separators .,/ python -m zarrcurator.synthetic_store –output-dir /tmp/all –separators .,/ –shards 4,4,8 –layouts flat,tree

Functions

store_variant_tag()

Return the tag of a store variant in store names, e.g. ‘z2’, ‘z2slash’, ‘z3shard’, ‘z3dotshardtree’.

Only what differs from the default (format default separator, no sharding, flat) is added. The tag has no ‘’, as store names are split on ‘’ by the dispatcher.

create_synthetic_experiment()

Create an experiment directory containing multiple synthetic stores.

One set of stores is created per combination of zarr format, entry in separators (None: only the format default), sharding and entry in layouts (None: only ‘flat’). With shards, the zarr v3 stores are created both without and with sharding of the data variables. The variant is tagged in the store name, see store_variant_tag(), e.g. syntheticexp_P1D_000_z2slash.zarr or syntheticexp_P1D_000_z3shardtree.zarr.

mergeKerchunkReferences()

Merge the Kerchunk references of the tarballs of a zarr store into the references of the store.

The tarballs of a zarr store are parts of it: each holds some of its variables, or some of the chunks of a variable, along with the metadata of the store, its groups and its arrays and the coordinate variables it needs. So the references of the store are the union of the references of its tarballs. A chunk of a data variable is in one tarball; metadata and the chunks of coordinate variables are in several, and are kept once after checking that their content is the same. The consolidated metadata (‘.zmetadata’) is left out, as the parquet references hold their own.

Args: jsonFiles[list[str]]: Paths of the Kerchunk reference files (JSON) of the tarballs. Returns: dict: Merged references, key -> metadata content or [url, offset, size]. Raises: ValueError: If a key is found in two tarballs with a different content or location.

convertKerchunkReferenceFilesOfZarrStoreToParquet()

Convert given Kerchunk reference file to parquet file.

To generate the Kerchunk reference file in JSON format for the contents of the input tar archive. The references of all tarballs of the store are merged, see mergeKerchunkReferences(). The references are combined in the zarr v2 layout: for zarr v3 stores the zarr.json metadata is translated to zarr v2 metadata and the chunks are referenced unchanged, so only zarr v3 arrays with a zarr v2 equivalent are supported; sharded arrays are referenced by their inner chunks, read from the shard indexes. Stores with nested groups (e.g. written from an xarray DataTree) are opened from the parquet references with consolidated=True.

Args: tarFile[str]: Path of the tar archive. Returns: None.

Module: zarrmetadata

Source: src/zarrcurator/zarrmetadata.py

This module contains helpers for translating zarr v3 metadata (zarr.json) to zarr v2 metadata (.zgroup, .zarray, .zattrs), so that the chunks of zarr v3 stores can be referenced by Kerchunk, which combines references in the zarr v2 layout.

The chunk bytes are referenced unchanged, so only codecs with a zarr v2 equivalent are supported: the ‘bytes’ codec followed by at most one compressor. ‘transpose’ and chained compressors raise a ValueError.

Sharded arrays (‘sharding_indexed’ codec) are translated to zarr v2 arrays of their inner chunks: each shard ends (or starts) with an index of the offset and size of its inner chunks, which is read to reference each inner chunk as a byte range within the shard. The inner codecs follow the rules above; nested sharding raises a ValueError.

Functions

v3CodecsToV2()

Translate the codecs of a zarr v3 array to a zarr v2 compressor.

Args: list[dict]: The ‘codecs’ of the zarr v3 array metadata. Returns: tuple: (endian, compressor), endian being ‘little’ or ‘big’ and compressor the zarr v2 compressor configuration or None.

v3MetadataToV2()

Translate the zarr v3 metadata of a group or array to zarr v2 metadata files.

The dimension names become the ‘_ARRAY_DIMENSIONS’ attribute. xarray keeps the fill value in the ‘_FillValue’ attribute of zarr v3 arrays, in zarr v2 it is the array’s fill_value, which xarray reads as ‘_FillValue’. So an array without ‘_FillValue’ and a zero fill value gets no fill value; zarr v2 reads missing chunks (not written as they hold only the fill value) as zeros then as well. A non-zero fill value is kept so missing chunks read correctly, though xarray then masks it.

Args: dict: Content of a zarr v3 ‘zarr.json’ file. Returns: dict: zarr v2 file name (‘.zgroup’, ‘.zarray’, ‘.zattrs’) -> content.

v3ShardingLayout()

Get the layout of the shards of a sharded zarr v3 array.

Args: dict: Content of the zarr v3 ‘zarr.json’ file of an array. Returns: dict or None: None for an array without sharding, else ‘shape’ (of the array), ‘shard_shape’, ‘chunk_shape’ (of the inner chunks), ‘codecs’ (of the inner chunks), ‘index_location’ (‘start’ or ‘end’), ‘index_endian’, ‘index_checksum’ (bool) and ‘index_size’ (bytes).

shardChunkReferences()

Get the references of the inner chunks of a shard.

Args: list: Reference of the shard, [url, offset, size]. str: Dot-separated zarr v2 key of the shard, relative to the array, e.g. ‘1.0’. dict: Layout of the shards, see v3ShardingLayout(). callable: read_range(url, start, end) returning the bytes in [start, end) of url. Returns: list[tuple]: (dot-separated key of the inner chunk relative to the array, [url, offset, size]) for every inner chunk in the shard that is written and lies within the array. Raises: ValueError: If the checksum of the shard index does not match.

v3ChunkKeyToV2()

Translate a chunk key of a zarr v3 array, relative to the array, to the dot-separated zarr v2 form.

Args: str: Chunk key, e.g. ‘c/0/1’ or ‘c.0.1’ (‘default’ encoding) or ‘0/1’ (‘v2’ encoding). dict: The ‘chunk_key_encoding’ of the zarr v3 array metadata. Returns: str: zarr v2 chunk key, e.g. ‘0.1’.
